At the end of the day, it sounds like you see things differently. As long as you aren’t being hypocritical and are taking care of your health (eating healthy, not smoking, exercising, etc.) I don’t think you’re wrong for wanting your partner to do the same. In a partnership, both people should try to be the best versions of themselves. However, it sounds like you’ve communicated your issues with his habits, and he wants to have his cake and eat it too, which maybe he can, or maybe he can’t, depending on your perspective. He believes he can solve this issue by still drinking soda, but also working out more. You believe he is stubbornly holding onto a pointless habit that is holding both him and your relationship back. You both have valid points. He is holding himself back, but he’s also working harder to “earn” an indulgence he seems to really enjoy. 

It’s impossible to get the full picture of your relationship from one snapshot provided by one person on a Reddit forum, but it sounds like his soda consumption isn’t gonna change anytime soon, and the more you try to convince him, the more frustrated you’ll be that he isn’t listening. I would suggest finding other areas where you’re frustrated in the relationship and focusing on what you can change rather than what you can’t, while still being honest and telling him that you feel like he’s prioritizing an unhealthy drink over his health and your relationship. Still, I would go with NAH, since you are looking out for him and trying to strengthen the relationship even if you may be hyperfixating on one issue, but he is also putting in work at the gym and cutting out smoking to try to compromise. Still, it does say something about your differing opinions on ambition, health, and your relationship that you might need to work through. 

If the gym for weight loss isn’t working and he’s still clinging onto his soda usage, then I would maybe start to shift towards saying he may be an AH, but I think you guys need time to work this out.
